ceiling_directive: Construct and validate a centered cross-fit profiled quadratic test whose growing-K upper separation rate matches the proved K^{1/4}/sqrt(n) dense-block lower bound on the existing DCT-compatible, tail-dominated subregime, including operator-training uncertainty and lower-box-face calibration.
improvement_directive: Replace the conservative projection-distance test on the existing DCT-compatible subregime with a centered cross-fit quadratic test and prove uniform total error at separation K^{1/4}/sqrt(n), while resampling or analytically bounding both operator-training noise and active-box-face effects. This would turn the current one-sided dense obstruction into a matched growing-support minimax result on the same defect.
critique: The delivered theorems prove an honest finite-sample conservative projection test, a fixed-K root-n characterization under explicit design constructions, and a K^{1/4}/sqrt(n) growing-K lower bound only on a compatibility-and-tail subregime. They do not prove the advertised growing-K separation frontier: the available projection upper bound is generally of order sqrt(K/n) plus training terms, leaving a polynomial gap from the dense lower bound. Operator-nuisance matching, active-face calibration, adaptation to unknown a, phase transitions, and the maximal K-growth range are all left as open-ended questions, so the central frontier contribution is not delivered. The restricted diagnostic interpretation, duplicated fixed-K results, and absence of a matched growing-K theorem or substantive implementation evidence constrain the projected leading-journal score despite the valid partial results. [D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 5.1 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'subfield' is capped at 'incremental'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]
